tasks.spec:
You are a read-only research analyst. STRICTLY NO CHANGES: no file modifications outside your working directory, no git, no MCP, no skills, no network; write only ./report.md. This is exploration for a future build (T3/T9) - Ankit explicitly ruled nothing changes yet.

RULING TO IMPLEMENT (Ankit, 2026-08-03): when the pathway's extracted date and the gateway's raw-conversation date disagree at the WEEK level, the system asks the patient ONE clarifying question offering both dates ('Did you mean Thursday 08/06 or Thursday 08/13?'), instead of silently picking. Day-part-only disagreement searches the whole day. Unreadable raw authority falls back to pathway extraction. At most ONE clarify per conversation (never a loop). Ankit's framing: Bland usually extracts right; the confusion happens between the conversation and the webhook availability call - so the clarify should cost exactly one extra turn and only fire on real week-level conflicts.

QUESTION: what is the MINIMAL wiring to implement that, given what already exists?

SOURCES (read-only): (1) /home/ankit114/repos/gw-diag-snap/container/bland_gateway.py - the code NOW RUNNING in production (commit 7e20fb1). Map the existing conflict plumbing precisely: resolve_from_conversation returning ('conflict', ...) tuples, clamp_availability_range setting body['date_conflict'] and logging date_source=conflict - under exactly which conditions does that fire today, what does the availability response carry when it does, and what does it NOT yet compare (does it compare raw vs the pathway-extracted from/to in the request body at all?). Cite file:line for every claim. (2) /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/pathway-v92.json - search the node graph for any date-conflict/clarify node history (names like n_date_conflict), what nodes consume availability responses, and where a conflict question would live (which node asks, which edges route the two answers). (3) /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/SPEC-v91.md - search for prior date-conflict / clarify design language (the ticket says a restored n_date_conflict pattern existed historically).

WRITE ./report.md: sections EXISTING PLUMBING (what fires today, file:line); GAP (exactly what comparison/signal is missing for week-level pathway-vs-raw conflict detection); MINIMAL WIRING (the smallest change set: gateway side - detect week-level disagreement between body from/to and raw resolution, return a structured conflict with BOTH dates instead of overwriting; pathway side - the clarify node + two edges + the once-per-conversation guard; enumerate each piece with where it goes); COPY DRAFT (the one clarifying question, EN + note that ZH parity is required); RISKS (what could loop or over-ask, and the guard for each); TEST PLAN (harness scenarios that would prove it: agree->no question, week-conflict->one question->correct booking path, conflict-again->no second question). Machine line required: exactly one 'WIRING_SIZE: <n> gateway changes, <m> pathway nodes/edges' summary. Final message <=15 lines.
tasks.check: grep -qiE '^#+ *EXISTING PLUMBING|EXISTING PLUMBING' report.md || { echo 'FAIL: no EXISTING PLUMBING section'; exit 1; }; grep -q 'date_conflict' report.md || { echo 'FAIL: report never examines the existing date_conflict plumbing'; exit 1; }; grep -qE 'WIRING_SIZE: [0-9]+ gateway changes, [0-9]+ pathway' report.md || { echo 'FAIL: no WIRING_SIZE machine line'; exit 1; }; c=$(grep -cE 'bland_gateway\.py:[0-9]+|:[0-9]{3,4}' report.md); [ "$c" -ge 4 ] || { echo "FAIL: only $c file:line citations, need 4+"; exit 1; }; grep -qiE 'test plan' report.md || { echo 'FAIL: no TEST PLAN section'; exit 1; }; echo "PASS: $(grep -m1 'WIRING_SIZE:' report.md); $c citations"
tasks.verified: A read-only wiring study for the one-question clarify: what conflict plumbing production already has (cited at file:line), the exact gap, the smallest gateway+pathway change set, copy draft, loop guards, and the harness scenarios that would prove it - ready for the T3 spec with zero changes made.
